main_text.p: stum. Eligebantur ephori quinque quotannis in comitiis ex toto populo, suffragiis ejusdem populi, sine discrimine generis aut opum, sæpeque fiebat, ut etiam infimæ fortunæ homines ad hanc dignitatem eveherentur: quod notat & reprehendit Aristoteles. Erat enim ma-gistratus hic prorsus popularis ad tuen-dam communis populi libertatē com-paratus, & regum, senatusque, & aliorum, qui in civitate eminebant, potentiæ suspectæ ac periculosæ oppositus: ad cujus exemplar tribunitia potestas tuendæ libertati plebis contra opes confulum ac senatus patritiorumque Romæ videtur instituta. Atque hanc ob causam expetebantur maximè ad hoc munus ii, qui in populo erant ingeniis acribus, ac libertatis amantibus, & potentium gratiæ cedere nescii. Verum accidit heic, quod Romæ circa munus tribunitium. Nam potestas modica initio, cum temporis progressu, crescente ephororum ambitione, modum fere ex-cessit, & reipublicæ formam aristocraticam in democraticam propemodum convertit: quod ex subjectis patescet. Erat iis curia in urbis foro sita, ut ex Paufaniâ recitatum, juxta regum & senatus curiam, & in hac sellas quinque pari cum ipsis numero, Ἀ[?]φος ἐφόρων[?] ἄunca[?]

page.notes: The Greek words at the end of the last line are only partly legible; the transcription is uncertain. The catchword at the lower right is read as "sunca" with doubt. The page number is read as 191 and may be 192. Show-through and frame lines at the left and right edges and the faint text at the lower left ("ipi", "ibydi") are not printed text on this page and are left out. The long s is written as plain s throughout. Printed hyphens at line ends are kept.
